title: The Phenytoin That Was Free — Merritt & Putnam Hydantoin Screen, State-Dependent NaV Inactivation, Michaelis–Menten Capacity-Limited CYP2C9 Clearance (PDB 1R9O), ICU Hypoalbuminemia Winter–Tozer Limits & Direct Ultrafiltration LC–MS/MS

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Ninety percent of phenytoin rides bound to blood albumin, while only the 10% 'free' unbound fraction enters the brain. In sick ICU patients with low albumin and saturable CYP2C9 clearance (PDB 1R9O), a 'normal' total level can hide severe phenytoin toxicity.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Treating the total blood number instead of the unbound concentration in hypoalbuminemic or renal-failure patients can cause clinicians to give *more* phenytoin to a patient who is already toxic.
keyTakeaways: Phenytoin stabilizes inactivated voltage-gated sodium channels and follows non-linear Michaelis–Menten pharmacokinetics because hepatic CYP2C9 (PDB 1R9O) saturates right inside the therapeutic range.
Because phenytoin is ~90% albumin-bound, low serum albumin or uremic displacers double the pharmacologically active unbound fraction while total serum concentration looks deceptively normal.
The Winter–Tozer equation estimates corrected phenytoin, but in multi-organ ICU illness direct ultrafiltration + LC–MS/MS free phenytoin measurement (therapeutic 1–2 mcg/mL) is the gold standard.

vocab.meaning: Capacity-limited metabolism where small dose increases above enzyme saturation cause disproportionately huge jumps in drug levels.
The percentage of drug not attached to plasma proteins like albumin—the only fraction free to cross into brain tissue or liver enzymes.
Spinning plasma through a molecular-weight membrane at 37 °C to physically separate protein-free drug before mass spectrometry.

quiz.question: An ICU patient with serum albumin of 1.8 g/dL has a total phenytoin level of 14 mcg/mL (reference 10–20) alongside nystagmus and ataxia. What is happening?
options: The phenytoin dose is too low
Low albumin has elevated the unbound active phenytoin concentration into the toxic range (>2 mcg/mL) despite a 'normal' total number
quiz.explanation: With fewer albumin binding sites, a total level of 14 mcg/mL corresponds to roughly double the normal free concentration, explaining clinical neurotoxicity.
